description: This topic explains the main forms of business ownership in Tanzania, including their formation, features, sources of capital, advantages and disadvantages, and the factors a person considers when choosing one.

mcq.questionText: A business that is owned and controlled by only one person is called a:
mcq.explanation: A sole proprietorship (sole trader) is owned, financed and controlled by a single person who keeps all the profit and bears all the risk.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the MAIN disadvantage of a sole proprietorship?

options.text: Profits are shared among many owners
Decisions are slow because of many owners
The owner has unlimited liability for business debts
It must publish its accounts to the public

mcq.explanation: A sole trader has unlimited liability, meaning personal property can be sold to pay business debts if the business fails.

mcq.questionText: The minimum number of people needed to form an ordinary partnership is:
mcq.explanation: A partnership is formed by a minimum of two persons who agree to carry on a business together to make profit.

mcq.questionText: The document that contains the terms and conditions agreed upon by partners is called the:
mcq.explanation: The partnership deed (agreement) sets out matters such as capital contributed, profit sharing ratio and duties of each partner.

mcq.questionText: A partner who contributes capital and shares profit but does NOT take part in the daily management of the business is called a:
mcq.explanation: A sleeping (dormant) partner invests capital and shares profit but does not participate in running the business.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a feature of a limited liability company?

options.text: It has no separate legal existence from its owners
Owners can lose their personal property to pay company debts
It is a separate legal person that can own property and be sued
It is owned by only one person

mcq.explanation: A limited company has a separate legal personality (it is an artificial person) distinct from its shareholders.

mcq.questionText: The owners of a limited liability company are known as:
mcq.explanation: People who buy shares in a company become shareholders and are the owners of that company.

mcq.questionText: A major difference between a private limited company and a public limited company is that a public limited company:

options.text: Can sell its shares to the general public
Cannot have more than fifty members
Is owned by the government only

mcq.explanation: A public limited company may invite the general public to buy its shares, often through a stock exchange, while a private company cannot.

mcq.questionText: Limited liability means that, if a company fails, a shareholder can lose:

options.text: All personal property including houses and cars
Only the amount of money paid for the shares
Twice the amount invested as a penalty

mcq.explanation: Limited liability protects shareholders; their loss is limited to the value of the shares they bought, not their personal property.

mcq.questionText: SACCOS in Tanzania is an example of which form of business ownership?
mcq.explanation: A SACCOS (Savings and Credit Cooperative Society) is a type of cooperative society where members save together and borrow from their pooled funds.

mcq.questionText: In a cooperative society, control is based on the principle of:

options.text: One shareholder, one vote per share
One member, one vote regardless of shares held
Voting power given only to the government
Voting power given only to the manager

mcq.explanation: Cooperatives follow democratic control: each member has one vote no matter how many shares they own.

mcq.questionText: A business that is owned and run by the government to provide essential services is called a:
mcq.explanation: A public corporation (parastatal) is a state-owned enterprise set up to provide essential goods and services, such as TANESCO supplying electricity.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the MAIN source of capital for a sole proprietorship?

options.text: Sale of shares to the public
Issue of debentures on the stock exchange

mcq.explanation: A sole trader mainly relies on personal savings, profits ploughed back, and small loans from banks or relatives.

mcq.questionText: Which form of business ownership usually finds it EASIEST to raise large amounts of capital?
mcq.explanation: A public limited company can sell shares to the general public, so it can raise very large amounts of capital compared with the other forms.

mcq.questionText: Which document must be submitted to register (incorporate) a limited liability company?
mcq.explanation: To form a company, promoters must prepare the Memorandum of Association and the Articles of Association and submit them for incorporation.

fib.questionText: A business owned and controlled by one person is called a _____.
fib.explanation: The sole proprietorship (sole trader) is the simplest form of business, owned by one person.

fib.questionText: The legal document that states the terms agreed by partners is the partnership _____.
fib.explanation: The partnership deed records capital contributions, profit sharing and the rights and duties of partners.

fib.questionText: A partner who contributes capital but does not take part in daily management is called a _____ partner.
fib.explanation: A sleeping or dormant partner provides capital and shares profit but does not manage the business.

fib.questionText: The owners of a limited liability company are called _____.
fib.explanation: Shareholders own the company through the shares they have purchased.

fib.questionText: When a shareholder can only lose the amount paid for their shares, this protection is called _____ liability.
fib.explanation: Limited liability restricts a shareholder's loss to the value of the shares held.

fib.questionText: A company that sells its shares to the general public is called a _____ limited company.
fib.explanation: A public limited company invites the public to buy shares, unlike a private limited company.

fib.questionText: A type of cooperative where members save money and borrow loans together is known by the short form _____.
fib.explanation: SACCOS stands for Savings and Credit Cooperative Society, common in Tanzania.

fib.questionText: A business owned and operated by the government to provide essential services is called a public _____.
fib.explanation: A public corporation (parastatal), such as TANESCO, is owned by the government.

fib.questionText: In a cooperative society, each member has _____ vote regardless of the number of shares owned.
fib.explanation: Democratic control means one member, one vote in cooperatives.

fib.questionText: The two main formation documents of a limited company are the Memorandum of Association and the _____ of Association.
fib.explanation: The Articles of Association set out the internal rules for running the company.

tf.questionText: A sole proprietor enjoys limited liability for the debts of the business.
tf.explanation: A sole proprietor has unlimited liability; personal assets can be used to pay business debts.

tf.questionText: A partnership can be formed by a minimum of two people.
tf.explanation: An ordinary partnership requires at least two persons to agree to run a business together.

tf.questionText: A limited liability company is a separate legal person from its shareholders.
tf.explanation: A company has its own legal personality and can own property, sue and be sued in its own name.

tf.questionText: A private limited company can freely sell its shares to the general public.
tf.explanation: Only a public limited company may sell shares to the general public; a private company cannot.

tf.questionText: In a cooperative society, the member with the most shares automatically has the most votes.
tf.explanation: Cooperatives use one member, one vote, so voting does not depend on the number of shares.

tf.questionText: TANESCO is an example of a public corporation in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: TANESCO is a government-owned public corporation that supplies electricity.

tf.questionText: A sole proprietorship usually finds it easier to raise large capital than a public limited company.
tf.explanation: A sole trader has limited sources of capital, while a public limited company can sell shares to the public to raise large funds.

tf.questionText: A sleeping partner takes part in the daily running of the partnership business.
tf.explanation: A sleeping partner only contributes capital and shares profit; they do not manage the business.

tf.questionText: Profits of a sole proprietorship are taken entirely by the single owner.
tf.explanation: Because the sole trader owns the business alone, all profits belong to them.

tf.questionText: A partnership deed must always be a written document; an oral agreement is never allowed.
tf.explanation: A partnership can be based on an oral agreement, though a written deed is strongly recommended to avoid disputes.

summary.questionText: State two advantages of a sole proprietorship.
summary.correctAnswer: Easy and cheap to start; the owner keeps all profits and makes quick decisions.
summary.explanation: Sole proprietorships are simple to form and give the owner full control and all the profit.

summary.questionText: State two disadvantages of a sole proprietorship.
summary.correctAnswer: Unlimited liability and difficulty in raising large capital.
summary.explanation: The owner risks personal property and has limited sources of finance.

summary.questionText: What is a partnership deed and what does it contain?
summary.correctAnswer: It is the written agreement among partners showing capital contributed, profit sharing ratio, and duties of each partner.
summary.explanation: The deed guides how the partnership is run and helps prevent disputes.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between a general partner and a limited partner.
summary.correctAnswer: A general partner has unlimited liability and manages the business, while a limited partner's liability is limited to capital contributed and does not manage.
summary.explanation: Limited partners protect their personal assets but give up management rights.

summary.questionText: Explain the meaning of limited liability.
summary.correctAnswer: It means a shareholder can only lose the amount paid for their shares and not their personal property if the company fails.
summary.explanation: Limited liability encourages investment by reducing the risk to owners.

summary.questionText: Give two differences between a private and a public limited company.
summary.correctAnswer: A private company cannot sell shares to the public and has fewer members, while a public company can sell shares to the public and has many members.
summary.explanation: These differences affect how each company raises capital and is controlled.

summary.questionText: What is a cooperative society? Give one Tanzanian example.
summary.correctAnswer: It is a voluntary association of people who join to meet common economic needs, for example a SACCOS or a coffee marketing cooperative.
summary.explanation: Cooperatives are member-owned and democratically controlled.

summary.questionText: Why does the government form public corporations?
summary.correctAnswer: To provide essential services, control key industries, and avoid private monopolies, for example supplying water and electricity.
summary.explanation: Public corporations serve the public interest where private firms may fail to.

summary.questionText: List three sources of capital for a limited liability company.
summary.correctAnswer: Sale of shares, bank loans, and issue of debentures or retained profits.
summary.explanation: Companies have wider sources of finance than sole traders or partnerships.

summary.questionText: Mention three factors to consider when choosing a form of business ownership.
summary.correctAnswer: The amount of capital needed, the degree of liability/risk, and the level of control desired.
summary.explanation: Other factors include legal requirements, continuity, and how profits will be shared.

hoq.questionText: Asha runs a small tailoring shop alone using her savings. As her business grows she needs much more capital and wants to protect her house from business debts, but she still wants to keep close control. Which form of ownership best fits her needs?

options.text: Form a private limited company with a few trusted members
Form a general partnership with unlimited liability

hoq.explanation: A private limited company gives limited liability (protecting her house), allows more capital from a few members, and still lets her keep close control without selling shares to the public.

hoq.questionText: A coffee marketing cooperative and a public limited company both sell agricultural produce. Which statement BEST explains a key difference in how they are controlled?

options.text: Both give voting power according to the number of shares held
The cooperative gives one vote per member while the company gives votes according to shares held
The company is democratically controlled while the cooperative is not
Both are controlled directly by the government

hoq.explanation: Cooperatives use one member, one vote (democratic control), while a company's voting power is tied to the number of shares each shareholder owns.

hoq.questionText: Two friends start a hardware business as a general partnership. One friend secretly takes a large business loan and the business fails owing a big debt. What is the position of the other partner?

options.text: He loses nothing because only the borrowing partner is liable
He can be held personally liable for the whole debt due to unlimited liability
He only loses his shares as in a limited company
The government pays the debt because it is a partnership

hoq.explanation: In a general partnership partners have unlimited liability and are jointly and severally liable, so one partner can be made to pay the full debt even from personal property.
